clue.text: Weaver's kit first used by driver

parts.note: Nick Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
kit means gear, equipment

explanation.surface: A loom-worker's equipment gets its first outing in the hands of a coach driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weaver' suggests a textile trade, but it is Bottom, the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist pulls away from rest in the lowest ratio of the gearbox, so it is the one engaged first.

clue.text: Early title to demonstrate our system

definitions.meaning: an old Irish earldom, created in the seventeenth century
a device used to show how the planets of the solar system move

explanation.surface: An old name given to show off how our system works.
explanation.walkthrough: The planetary model was named after Charles Boyle, Earl of that title, for whom one was made.
explanation.definitionFit: A clockwork planetary model shows the solar system's workings, and its name comes from an Irish earl's title.

clue.text: Tension builds up to the French in race on the loch

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the loch comes after
in places the French phrase inside the race

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
au is French for to the
Loch Ness, Scotland's famous loch

explanation.surface: Stress mounts as French competitors race on a Scottish loch.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race; 'builds up' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tautness is the state of being pulled tight, which is tension.

clue.text: Disposed of by Act of Union?

definitions.text: Disposed of by Act of Union?

parts.words: Disposed of by Act of Union?
parts.note: not the parliamentary Act uniting nations but the wedding by which parents find a husband or wife for a child

explanation.surface: A historic statute merging nations got rid of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act of Union' suggests the treaties joining England, Scotland and Ireland; here it is a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Parents who find a spouse for a daughter are said to have got her settled through wedlock, so disposed of by a union.

clue.text: Rival bird, a variety of teal

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: a variety of means the letters of the duck name are given in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A competing bird turns out to be a kind of teal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a variety of' rearranges TEAL into LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rival someone is to try to equal or match them, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Plane inclined to gain altitude

parts.note: not an aircraft climbing but a sloping surface used to go up a level

explanation.surface: An aircraft tilts upward to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' looks like an aircraft, but it is a flat surface; an inclined plane takes you higher.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloping walkway or road linking two levels is an inclined plane for going up.

clue.text: Kingston's on the horizon — can't see the river

definitions.text: Kingston's on the horizon — can't see the river

parts.words: Kingston's on the horizon — can't see the river
parts.note: Kingston upon Hull is named after its river; when a ship is far off, its body is below the horizon and out of sight

explanation.surface: A sailor sees the town of Kingston on the horizon, but the river is out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingston upon Hull, the English port, is usually called Hull, also the name of its river and of a ship's body.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship far off whose body is below the horizon, only its masts visible, is described this way.

clue.text: Some hitches with this leg of mutton

definitions.meaning: a knot used for shortening a rope, one of the hitches sailors tie
the lower leg of a sheep

explanation.surface: A cook ties knots round a leg of lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sailor's knot for shortening rope, and literally names the shin of the animal that gives mutton.

clue.text: Waylay a double-decker in Newham

indicators.note: in places the vehicle inside the rearranged letters of ham

parts.note: the London borough's name is read as 'new HAM', the letters of ham in a new order
a double-decker is a London bus

explanation.surface: Someone lies in wait for a London double-decker in an East London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: Newham is split as NEW + HAM, with 'new' telling you to rearrange HAM into AMH; 'a' is only the article before the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: To waylay someone is to lie in wait and attack them by surprise, a synonym.

clue.text: Sound made by forming fours?

indicators.note: forming means the two copies of the number word are shaped into something new

parts.note: the plural gives the word four twice over

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant's order to form fours makes a certain noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forming fours' is a parade-ground drill command, but 'forming' rearranges two copies of FOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustling or swishing noise, as of silk skirts, is called this, so it is a kind of sound.

clue.text: Oral application useful to, a chap

definitions.meaning: helpful to someone with a chapped mouth, read as 'a chap(ped lip)'

explanation.surface: A balm for the mouth comes in handy for a fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chap' looks like a man, but here it is the noun for a crack in dry skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A balm smeared on the mouth soothes cracked skin, so it serves as an oral ointment and helps with chapping.

clue.text: Bond formed by dancing, say

indicators.note: say tells us the dance word is spoken, matching a word spelt differently

parts.note: jive is a lively style of dancing

explanation.surface: A tie is formed between partners through dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word means a shackle or fetter, and a fetter is a bond.

clue.text: Underground majority of voters may betray Radicals

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing on someone
radical comes from Latin radix, root, so radicals are roots

explanation.surface: The secret mass of the electorate may sell out the Radical party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for informing to the police; 'Underground' is part of the definition, as roots lie below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinary rank-and-file members of a party or electorate are called this, and roots lie below the surface.

clue.text: Site a storm damaged — they assess the cost

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of the preceding words are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Loss adjusters visit a location wrecked by a storm to cost the repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: People who estimate prices, as builders do when quoting, assess costs.

clue.text: Lucifer in top form may decide the issue

parts.note: a lucifer is an old word for a friction match
a top or tip is a point

explanation.surface: The Devil at his best might settle the dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lucifer' looks like Satan, but it is an old name for a match; 'in ... form' links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, the point that would win the whole contest can settle its outcome.

clue.text: Shelley's nemesis a final alternative

parts.note: final means last
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A last option for the poet Shelley's avenging fate.
explanation.walkthrough: Shelley wrote a poem of this name; in Greek myth it is an avenging spirit, hence a nemesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was an avenging spirit, and Shelley titled a poem after it, so it is a nemesis in his work.

clue.text: Gain ally by negotiating reduction

indicators.note: negotiating means working the words over, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diplomat wins a partner by bargaining for a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing or lessening pain or fears is a lowering of them, a gerund used as a noun for diminution.

clue.text: Apple-picker suffers a loss in Georgian city

indicators.note: suffers a loss means one letter A is dropped from the heroine's name

parts.note: Atalanta, the swift huntress of Greek myth, lost a race by stopping to pick up golden apples

explanation.surface: Someone harvesting apples has a setback in a city in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: Atalanta stooped for the golden apples Hippomenes threw; lose one A from her name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the state capital of Georgia in the USA.

clue.text: Stress alternative name for the dunnock

parts.note: stress on a syllable is its accent
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Emphasis on another name for a small brown hedge bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative name' reads as one phrase, but 'alternative' gives OR and 'name for' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The hedge sparrow, a small brown British songbird, belongs to a family of birds called by this name.

clue.text: Light Division troop-leader heads charge winning liberation

indicators.note: heads means goes in front of the next piece

parts.note: the first letter of troop
a ransom is the price paid to free a captive

explanation.surface: An officer in the Light Division leads a charge that frees prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: The Light Division is a British army formation; here it is a crossbar dividing a window or a window above a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal bar separating panes of a window, or the window above a door, divides the light.

clue.text: Go out with aunt to the river

parts.note: Aunt Sally is a British pub game in which sticks are thrown at a dummy, so aunt suggests Sally
the Forth is a river in Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone takes their aunt for a walk down to the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a traditional British throwing game, hence aunt gives SALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out on a trip or venture is an idiom for leaving, going out.

clue.text: What might spoil the wine, see, in Ireland?

definitions.meaning: a stopper whose fungal taint makes wine '...'
a see is a bishop's diocese, here one in the Republic of Ireland

explanation.surface: A tasting in Ireland asks what could ruin the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle's stopper can taint wine, and an Irish city gives its name to a diocese.

clue.text: Office instruction was once generally read, they say

definitions.text: Office instruction was once generally read, they say

parts.words: Office instruction was once generally read, they say
parts.note: directions in a church service book were printed in red ink; 'read' said aloud sounds like that colour

explanation.surface: Office memos were once widely read, people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' is the church's daily service, not a workplace; such directions were printed in red, and 'read, they say' sounds like red.
explanation.definitionFit: A direction in a liturgical book, traditionally printed in red, tells the priest how to conduct a service.

clue.text: Paradoxical figure has little time, within a year, in Oxfordshire

indicators.note: in places that whole unit inside the county abbreviation

parts.note: Oxon is the standard abbreviation for Oxfordshire

indicators.note: within puts the short moment inside the abbreviated year

parts.note: yr is a short form of year
mo, short for moment, is a little time

explanation.surface: An odd character lives in Oxfordshire for a year but spends little time there.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech joining contradictory terms, like 'deafening silence', is paradoxical.

clue.text: So Lawrence was called to assist Somerville

definitions.meaning: T. E. Lawrence enlisted in the RAF under an assumed surname
Edith Somerville wrote Irish novels with her cousin Violet Martin, who used a pen name

explanation.surface: Lawrence was summoned to help a woman named Somerville.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence of Arabia used this alias in the RAF; Somerville and her cousin wrote as a duo under this name.
explanation.definitionFit: It was T. E. Lawrence's alias in the air force and the pen name of Edith Somerville's co-author.

clue.text: They move to follow up a section of the Act

definitions.text: They move to follow up a section of the Act

parts.words: They move to follow up a section of the Act
parts.note: a play's act is divided into scenes; stagehands move the scenery between one scene and the next

explanation.surface: Officials move to amend a clause of an Act of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' looks like legislation, but it is a part of a play, and its 'section' is a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Scene-changers in a theatre move scenery between scenes; the clue gives the second half of their name.

clue.text: The real sport of kings

parts.note: racing is usually called the sport of kings, but the indoor court game played by Henry VIII is 'real' (royal)

explanation.surface: A claim about which pastime truly belongs to monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Real' looks like 'genuine' but names the old royal court game, real ____; horse racing is the usual 'sport of kings'.
explanation.definitionFit: The original court game with rackets was played by French and English monarchs, hence a royal pastime.

clue.text: S African lepidoptera found victory with wings here

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
A is a standard abbreviation for African
the order of moths and butterflies, read as a whole race of moths

explanation.surface: South African butterflies discovered a winged victory in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The Winged Victory statue in the Louvre was unearthed on this Aegean island.
explanation.definitionFit: The marble Winged Victory, a statue of the goddess Nike, was discovered on this Greek island in 1863.
